chunk_findings.detail:
`added_lines` decides that a line is a file header purely by prefix (`line.startswith("+++ ")`) and never tracks whether it is currently inside a hunk body, so an *added content* line whose text begins with `++ ` is mistaken for a `+++ b/<path>` header and clobbers `path` for the rest of that file.

Concretely: take an existing extractor-surface file `src/util.py` (not a doc), and suppose the change adds, at line 11, any line whose text starts with `++ ` (e.g. a patch/test fixture or a quoted snippet such as `++ expected`), and also adds a new public function at line 40. `git diff -U0 base --` emits, for that file:

```
+++ b/src/util.py
@@ -10,0 +11 @@
+++ expected          <-- content line = "+" + "++ expected"
...
@@ -39,0 +40 @@        <-- the new function
+def foo(): ...
```

Because the content line `+++ expected` matches `line.startswith("+++ ")`, line 35 sets `path = "expected"` (line[4:] = `"expected"`). Every later hunk header in the same file is then parsed under the bogus path (line 39: `out.setdefault(path, set())`), so `added["src/util.py"]` never receives line 40, and `restrict` drops the extractor finding for the genuinely new symbol at line 40 — the check silently reports the new surface as documented/clean even though it was added by this diff. The correct behaviour requires only treating `+++ ` as a header when it is not a hunk body (e.g. anchor on the `diff --git`/`--- ` header pair or track hunk state).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_diff.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: `_verdict` only catches `urllib.error.URLError`/`OSError`/`ValueError`, but `urllib.request.urlopen` can raise `http.client.InvalidURL`, which is a subclass of `HTTPException(Exception)` and of neither `OSError` nor `ValueError`, so it escapes `_verdict` and `check_remote` entirely. Concretely, for a document containing `[bad](https://example.com:8080x/)` (any http(s) URL with a non-numeric port, e.g. a typo like `https://host:80oo/`, or an unclosed IPv6 literal like `https://[[REDACTED:ipv6]/`), `remote_links` returns that URL (it starts with `https://` and matches `_LINK`), so `_verdict` calls `urlopen`; `AbstractHTTPHandler.do_open` then constructs `HTTPSConnection(host, ...)` outside any OSError-wrapping try, and `HTTPConnection._get_hostport` raises `InvalidURL("nonnumeric port: '8080x'")`. That exception is not in the except tuple, so instead of being counted and making the result `unavailable` (the module's stated contract: a link that cannot be looked at is counted, never a silent pass and never a crash), the whole docs check aborts with an uncaught traceback. Note the sibling hazard on line 49: `urllib.request.Request(...)` is also built before the `try`, so any `ValueError` it raises would likewise escape; the `ValueError` in the tuple only covers the `urlopen` call. Either add `http.client.InvalidURL` (or a broad `Exception`) to the tuple or move construction/validation of the request inside the `try`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_net.py:51-55 (`_verdict`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`blocking` returns `self.severity == "block" and not self.report.clean`, and `report.clean` is the `Report`'s cleanliness, which only knows about findings. `unavailable` is a field on `Check`, so it can never make the result unclean. The field's own comment says "the check is not clean while this is set", and the module docstring says "a check that did not run is never a clean one" — yet nothing in this module turns `unavailable` into a non-clean/blocking result.

Concrete input: `[docs]` has `severity = "block"` and `lint_command = "definitely-not-a-real-binary"`, and the docs themselves have no findings. `_lint` sets `check.unavailable["lint"] = "`definitely-not-a-real-binary` did not run: ..."` and appends no `Finding`, so `report.clean` stays `True`, `check.blocking` is `False`, and `as_dict()` reports `"blocking": false` alongside `"unavailable": {...}`. Anything consuming `check.blocking` (or `check.report.clean`) to gate the docs therefore passes a run in which a configured check never executed, contradicting the stated invariant "unavailable never clean". The same happens for `check_links = "network"` when `check_remote` reports `remote.unavailable`.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/docscheck_run.py` — `Check.blocking` (used by `run_check`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`run_check` takes `run_commands: bool = True` and threads it into `check_configured`, but the `_lint` helper neither receives nor checks it; it calls `CommandRunner().run(...)` unconditionally. So a caller that explicitly disables command execution still has an arbitrary shell line executed.

Concrete input: `run_check(repo, cfg, run_commands=False)` with `[docs].lint_command = "git push origin main"` (or any slow/side-effecting command). The reference command checks are skipped, but the lint command is still spawned in `repo`, and its exit code is recorded (`report.checked["lint"] = 1` plus a `lint` finding on failure). The flag contract "do not run commands" is violated for exactly one of the two command paths in this module, so a dry-run/plan or test invocation actually mutates state and can fail the check.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/docscheck_run.py` — `_lint` ignores `run_commands`

chunk_findings.detail:
The file-header test is applied to every line of `done.out`, including hunk bodies. A body line for an *added* line is the marker `+` followed by the file's content, so if the added content itself begins with `++ ` the raw diff line begins with `+++ ` and is mistaken for a `+++ <path>` header.

Concrete input: a source file whose added content contains the line `++ counter` (valid Python: `++counter` with a space), e.g.

    @@ -1,0 +1,1 @@
    ++ counter
    @@ -40,0 +41,2 @@
    +def new_api(): ...
    +    ...

The parser sets `path = "counter"` on `++ counter`, so the second hunk's added lines 41–42 are recorded under the bogus key `"counter"` instead of the real file. `restrict` then sees the real file's findings at lines 41–42 whose line is not in `added[real]` (the set was truncated at line 1) and drops them, so `ddflow docs check --diff BASE` reports clean for a symbol the diff actually added. Because the whole point of `--diff` is to decide keep/drop by line, losing a hunk's line set is a silent false clean (the `@@` regex is safe here only because a hunk regex is anchored at `^@@` and every body line carries a `+`/`-`/space prefix; the `+++ ` test has no such protection).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_diff.py `added_lines` (the `if line.startswith("+++ ")` branch, ~line 34)

chunk_findings.detail:
Path extraction hard-codes the default `b/` prefix and assumes the path is unquoted. `git diff` honours `diff.mnemonicPrefix` (and `diff.noprefix`, and user `diff.dstPrefix`), and `-c core.quotepath=off` disables quoting only for non-ASCII bytes, not for `"`/`\`/control characters.

Concrete environment: with `git config --global diff.mnemonicPrefix true`, the header is `+++ w/ddflow/services/foo.py`; `removeprefix("b/")` is a no-op, so `added` is keyed by `w/ddflow/services/foo.py` while `Finding.path` is the repo-relative `ddflow/services/foo.py`. No key ever matches, every extractor finding fails the `elif f.path in added` test and `restrict` drops them all, so the check reports clean on an environment it could not actually read (the same silent-clean failure mode the OSError path exists to prevent). Forcing the prefixes (`--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`) or stripping the first path segment unconditionally would avoid it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_diff.py `added_lines` (`line[4:].removeprefix("b/")`, ~line 35)

chunk_findings.detail: `_verdict` only catches `HTTPError`, `URLError`/`OSError`/`ValueError`, but `urllib.request` raises `http.client.HTTPException` subclasses that are **not** `OSError` or `ValueError`, and `AbstractHTTPHandler.do_open` constructs the connection object outside its `except OSError` wrapper. So a syntactically broken-but-plausible markdown URL aborts the whole `ddflow docs check` with a traceback instead of yielding `unavailable`. Concrete input: a document containing `[x](http://example.com:abc/path)` (a typo'd port) or `[x](http://[[REDACTED:ipv6]/path)` (unclosed IPv6 bracket). `remote_links` captures it (it passes the `http://` prefix filter), `check_remote` calls `_verdict`, `http.client._get_hostport` raises `InvalidURL("nonnumeric port: 'abc'")`, none of the three `except` arms at line 53–56 match, and the exception escapes `check_remote` — the check neither records a `silent` result nor sets `RemoteResult.unavailable`, contradicting the module docstring and the "unavailable never clean" intent. Catching `http.client.InvalidURL`/`http.client.HTTPException` (mapping it to `"silent"`, i.e. unavailable) fixes it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_net.py:55

chunk_findings.detail: The property is defined as `return self.severity == "block" and not self.report.clean`, so it only ever looks at the *finding* side of the report and completely ignores `self.unavailable`, even though the field's own comment says "the check is not clean while this is set" and the stated intent of the change is "unavailable never clean". Concrete input: `[docs] severity = "block"`, a `lint_command` that `CommandRunner` cannot launch, and documents with no other defects. `_lint` then takes the `if not run.ran:` branch, sets `check.unavailable["lint"] = "`...` did not run: ..."` and appends **no** finding, so `report.clean` stays `True`; `blocking` returns `False`. `Check.as_dict()` consequently emits `"severity": "block", "blocking": false` together with a non-empty `"unavailable"`, and any consumer that keys the docs gate on `blocking` (the field documented as "the docs gate may not pass") lets the gate pass even though the configured check was skipped. The same happens for `check_links = "network"` when `check_remote` reports itself unavailable. To satisfy "unavailable never clean", `blocking` must also be true when `self.unavailable` is non-empty (and `severity == "block"`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_run.py `Check.blocking`

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard raises `OSError` for *any* `+++` line whose path git C-quotes, and the raise aborts the whole diff-scoped run (the caller turns `OSError` into "could not run"), even when the quoted file is not a doc and not in scope. This is reachable with ordinary inputs: git only suppresses C-quoting for non-ASCII (`core.quotepath=off`), and still quotes paths containing `"`, `\`, or control characters, so a repo holding a changed macOS-created asset such as `assets/banner"v2".png` (or a fixture named `a\b.md`) makes every `ddflow docs check --diff <base>` exit 2 with "git quotes a path in the diff of <base>; cannot read it", reporting nothing. Before this change the same diff produced a full report: the old code took `line[4:]` verbatim, yielding the harmless bogus key `"b/assets/banner\"v2\".png"`, which matches no doc path and therefore changed no result. The refusal is also broader than the concern it encodes (a quoted *doc* path being silently dropped from the added-lines map): it fires on non-doc files that `doc_globs`/`ignore_paths` exclude, and the `+++`/`/dev/null` branch right below shows the code already knows how to skip a path it does not want to attribute. Concrete failure: modify `assets/banner"v2".png` on top of `main`, run `ddflow docs check --diff main` — got exit 2 and no report, expected the normal report for the docs that actually changed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_diff.py:48 (the quoted-path guard in `added_lines`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The regenerated `[docs]` block documents exactly eight knobs — `docs.severity`, `docs.check_links`, `docs.link_timeout_s`, `docs.check_paths`, `docs.lint_command`, `docs.ignore_paths`, `docs.ignore_names`, and `docs.extract` — and `docs.cli_command` appears nowhere. The intent states, verbatim, that the copied `ddflow/config_sections/docs.py` DocsConfig is `severity`, `check_links`, `check_paths`, `lint_command`, `cli_command` (read by B-docscheck-extractors), `ignore_paths`, `ignore_names`, `extract`, i.e. a set that contains `cli_command` and does not contain `link_timeout_s`. These two eight-element sets cannot both be correct, and each possible resolution is a defect:

* If the section really defines `cli_command` but no `link_timeout_s`, the golden was hand-edited / not regenerated from the code, so `test_golden_outputs` fails the first time `config --explain` runs (the explain output would print `docs.cli_command = ''` and would not print `docs.link_timeout_s`).
* If the section instead defines `link_timeout_s` in place of `cli_command`, commit 8209c908/09ebbddd was rewritten rather than copied as instructed, and B-docscheck-extractors' "`cli_command`" reader has no knob to read; the README claim of "228 knobs across 31 sections" (220 + the 8 enumerated knobs, `cli_command` included) is then wrong by one, since the docs section would contribute `link_timeout_s` as a ninth-or-substituted knob and the knob_added fragment set required by the release-manifest lint would not match the documented knobs.

Concretely, given a `Config` whose `docs` section is the one specified (`cli_command` present), line 1982ff of this snapshot produces a `docs` listing containing `docs.link_timeout_s = 10` and no `docs.cli_command`; snapshot comparison fails because the produced explain output differs in both directions (extra key, missing key). The change needs to show which of the two knob sets the code actually has, and make the golden, the README counts and the knob fragments ag
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr (`docs.link_timeout_s` / missing `docs.cli_command`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new test configures `[docs] severity = "block"` together with a `lint_command` that cannot run (`"no-such-linter-xyz"`), then asserts both that the report is not clean / is blocking **and** that `out.exit == O.NOTHING` (the no-finding exit code, i.e. 0). That contradicts the exit contract this task is defined by: `Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 could not run (never 0) / 3 refused`. Here a configured check literally could not run and the report is explicitly not clean (`out.data["clean"] is False`) and blocking (`out.data["blocking"] is True`), so the run is exactly the "could not run"/refused case that must not be reported as 0; a CI job that inspects only the exit status of `ddflow docs check` would treat a blocking, could-not-run report as a pass. The test locks in that behaviour, so either the assertion should expect the non-zero outcome (2/3) or the implementation's exit mapping is wrong — the test as written enshrines exit 0 for the case the intent says must never be 0.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_docs_check_command.py::test_block_also_holds_when_a_configured_check_could_not_run

chunk_findings.detail:
The new golden output for `["help"], 0` no longer just bumps the count (114 → 115) and appends `ddflow_docs` to a proper category. It appends a brand-new section whose header is the literal string `Unmapped — add a prefix to `_GROUPS``, with `ddflow_docs` nested underneath:

```
Help
  ddflow_help
Unmapped — add a prefix to `_GROUPS`
  ddflow_docs
```

That header is an imperative addressed to a developer (`add a prefix to _GROUPS`), not user-facing text; it appears here only because the new `ddflow_docs` tool was never registered in `_GROUPS`, so the help generator falls through to its "unmapped" bucket. Before this change every tool was mapped and the section was absent — this change is what introduces it. Anyone running `ddflow help` (the exact command this transcript captures) now sees an internal TODO instead of `ddflow_docs` sitting in a real category such as the "Looking at it"/docs group. Re-pinning the transcript to accept the unmapped entry encodes the regression rather than fixing it; the `_GROUPS` table needs a `ddflow_docs` entry (or a `docs` prefix) and the transcript should be re-pinned from that state.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (the repinned `ddflow help` blob)

chunk_findings.detail:
The regenerated `help index` transcript shows that the newly added MCP/CLI tool `ddflow_docs` is not registered in the help grouping table `_GROUPS`: the index now ends with a brand-new section

```
Unmapped — add a prefix to `_GROUPS`
  ddflow_docs
```

No such section exists in the previous transcript, so this change is what introduced it. The consequence is user-visible: any `ddflow help index` (CLI or MCP) now prints an internal developer instruction ("add a prefix to `_GROUPS`") and files the new docs tool under "Unmapped" instead of a real topic group, e.g. "Looking at it" / config. The tool count line was correctly bumped (114 → 115) but the grouping was not updated, so the diff now encodes a help-output regression. Add `ddflow_docs` to the appropriate `_GROUPS` entry and regenerate this transcript.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (help index / `_GROUPS`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`added_lines` decides that a line is a file header purely by prefix (`line.startswith("+++ ")`) and never tracks whether it is currently inside a hunk body, so an *added content* line whose text begins with `++ ` is mistaken for a `+++ b/<path>` header and clobbers `path` for the rest of that file.

Concretely: take an existing extractor-surface file `src/util.py` (not a doc), and suppose the change adds, at line 11, any line whose text starts with `++ ` (e.g. a patch/test fixture or a quoted snippet such as `++ expected`), and also adds a new public function at line 40. `git diff -U0 base --` emits, for that file:

```
+++ b/src/util.py
@@ -10,0 +11 @@
+++ expected          <-- content line = "+" + "++ expected"
...
@@ -39,0 +40 @@        <-- the new function
+def foo(): ...
```

Because the content line `+++ expected` matches `line.startswith("+++ ")`, line 35 sets `path = "expected"` (line[4:] = `"expected"`). Every later hunk header in the same file is then parsed under the bogus path (line 39: `out.setdefault(path, set())`), so `added["src/util.py"]` never receives line 40, and `restrict` drops the extractor finding for the genuinely new symbol at line 40 — the check silently reports the new surface as documented/clean even though it was added by this diff. The correct behaviour requires only treating `+++ ` as a header when it is not a hunk body (e.g. anchor on the `diff --git`/`--- ` header pair or track hunk state).

chunk_findings.detail: `_verdict` only catches `urllib.error.URLError`/`OSError`/`ValueError`, but `urllib.request.urlopen` can raise `http.client.InvalidURL`, which is a subclass of `HTTPException(Exception)` and of neither `OSError` nor `ValueError`, so it escapes `_verdict` and `check_remote` entirely. Concretely, for a document containing `[bad](https://example.com:8080x/)` (any http(s) URL with a non-numeric port, e.g. a typo like `https://host:80oo/`, or an unclosed IPv6 literal like `https://[[REDACTED:ipv6]/`), `remote_links` returns that URL (it starts with `https://` and matches `_LINK`), so `_verdict` calls `urlopen`; `AbstractHTTPHandler.do_open` then constructs `HTTPSConnection(host, ...)` outside any OSError-wrapping try, and `HTTPConnection._get_hostport` raises `InvalidURL("nonnumeric port: '8080x'")`. That exception is not in the except tuple, so instead of being counted and making the result `unavailable` (the module's stated contract: a link that cannot be looked at is counted, never a silent pass and never a crash), the whole docs check aborts with an uncaught traceback. Note the sibling hazard on line 49: `urllib.request.Request(...)` is also built before the `try`, so any `ValueError` it raises would likewise escape; the `ValueError` in the tuple only covers the `urlopen` call. Either add `http.client.InvalidURL` (or a broad `Exception`) to the tuple or move construction/validation of the request inside the `try`.

chunk_findings.detail:
The file-header test is applied to every line of `done.out`, including hunk bodies. A body line for an *added* line is the marker `+` followed by the file's content, so if the added content itself begins with `++ ` the raw diff line begins with `+++ ` and is mistaken for a `+++ <path>` header.

Concrete input: a source file whose added content contains the line `++ counter` (valid Python: `++counter` with a space), e.g.

    @@ -1,0 +1,1 @@
    ++ counter
    @@ -40,0 +41,2 @@
    +def new_api(): ...
    +    ...

The parser sets `path = "counter"` on `++ counter`, so the second hunk's added lines 41–42 are recorded under the bogus key `"counter"` instead of the real file. `restrict` then sees the real file's findings at lines 41–42 whose line is not in `added[real]` (the set was truncated at line 1) and drops them, so `ddflow docs check --diff BASE` reports clean for a symbol the diff actually added. Because the whole point of `--diff` is to decide keep/drop by line, losing a hunk's line set is a silent false clean (the `@@` regex is safe here only because a hunk regex is anchored at `^@@` and every body line carries a `+`/`-`/space prefix; the `+++ ` test has no such protection).

chunk_findings.detail:
Path extraction hard-codes the default `b/` prefix and assumes the path is unquoted. `git diff` honours `diff.mnemonicPrefix` (and `diff.noprefix`, and user `diff.dstPrefix`), and `-c core.quotepath=off` disables quoting only for non-ASCII bytes, not for `"`/`\`/control characters.

Concrete environment: with `git config --global diff.mnemonicPrefix true`, the header is `+++ w/ddflow/services/foo.py`; `removeprefix("b/")` is a no-op, so `added` is keyed by `w/ddflow/services/foo.py` while `Finding.path` is the repo-relative `ddflow/services/foo.py`. No key ever matches, every extractor finding fails the `elif f.path in added` test and `restrict` drops them all, so the check reports clean on an environment it could not actually read (the same silent-clean failure mode the OSError path exists to prevent). Forcing the prefixes (`--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`) or stripping the first path segment unconditionally would avoid it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_verdict` only catches `HTTPError`, `URLError`/`OSError`/`ValueError`, but `urllib.request` raises `http.client.HTTPException` subclasses that are **not** `OSError` or `ValueError`, and `AbstractHTTPHandler.do_open` constructs the connection object outside its `except OSError` wrapper. So a syntactically broken-but-plausible markdown URL aborts the whole `ddflow docs check` with a traceback instead of yielding `unavailable`. Concrete input: a document containing `[x](http://example.com:abc/path)` (a typo'd port) or `[x](http://[[REDACTED:ipv6]/path)` (unclosed IPv6 bracket). `remote_links` captures it (it passes the `http://` prefix filter), `check_remote` calls `_verdict`, `http.client._get_hostport` raises `InvalidURL("nonnumeric port: 'abc'")`, none of the three `except` arms at line 53–56 match, and the exception escapes `check_remote` — the check neither records a `silent` result nor sets `RemoteResult.unavailable`, contradicting the module docstring and the "unavailable never clean" intent. Catching `http.client.InvalidURL`/`http.client.HTTPException` (mapping it to `"silent"`, i.e. unavailable) fixes it.

chunk_findings.detail: The property is defined as `return self.severity == "block" and not self.report.clean`, so it only ever looks at the *finding* side of the report and completely ignores `self.unavailable`, even though the field's own comment says "the check is not clean while this is set" and the stated intent of the change is "unavailable never clean". Concrete input: `[docs] severity = "block"`, a `lint_command` that `CommandRunner` cannot launch, and documents with no other defects. `_lint` then takes the `if not run.ran:` branch, sets `check.unavailable["lint"] = "`...` did not run: ..."` and appends **no** finding, so `report.clean` stays `True`; `blocking` returns `False`. `Check.as_dict()` consequently emits `"severity": "block", "blocking": false` together with a non-empty `"unavailable"`, and any consumer that keys the docs gate on `blocking` (the field documented as "the docs gate may not pass") lets the gate pass even though the configured check was skipped. The same happens for `check_links = "network"` when `check_remote` reports itself unavailable. To satisfy "unavailable never clean", `blocking` must also be true when `self.unavailable` is non-empty (and `severity == "block"`).

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard raises `OSError` for *any* `+++` line whose path git C-quotes, and the raise aborts the whole diff-scoped run (the caller turns `OSError` into "could not run"), even when the quoted file is not a doc and not in scope. This is reachable with ordinary inputs: git only suppresses C-quoting for non-ASCII (`core.quotepath=off`), and still quotes paths containing `"`, `\`, or control characters, so a repo holding a changed macOS-created asset such as `assets/banner"v2".png` (or a fixture named `a\b.md`) makes every `ddflow docs check --diff <base>` exit 2 with "git quotes a path in the diff of <base>; cannot read it", reporting nothing. Before this change the same diff produced a full report: the old code took `line[4:]` verbatim, yielding the harmless bogus key `"b/assets/banner\"v2\".png"`, which matches no doc path and therefore changed no result. The refusal is also broader than the concern it encodes (a quoted *doc* path being silently dropped from the added-lines map): it fires on non-doc files that `doc_globs`/`ignore_paths` exclude, and the `+++`/`/dev/null` branch right below shows the code already knows how to skip a path it does not want to attribute. Concrete failure: modify `assets/banner"v2".png` on top of `main`, run `ddflow docs check --diff main` — got exit 2 and no report, expected the normal report for the docs that actually changed.

chunk_findings.detail:
The regenerated `[docs]` block documents exactly eight knobs — `docs.severity`, `docs.check_links`, `docs.link_timeout_s`, `docs.check_paths`, `docs.lint_command`, `docs.ignore_paths`, `docs.ignore_names`, and `docs.extract` — and `docs.cli_command` appears nowhere. The intent states, verbatim, that the copied `ddflow/config_sections/docs.py` DocsConfig is `severity`, `check_links`, `check_paths`, `lint_command`, `cli_command` (read by B-docscheck-extractors), `ignore_paths`, `ignore_names`, `extract`, i.e. a set that contains `cli_command` and does not contain `link_timeout_s`. These two eight-element sets cannot both be correct, and each possible resolution is a defect:

* If the section really defines `cli_command` but no `link_timeout_s`, the golden was hand-edited / not regenerated from the code, so `test_golden_outputs` fails the first time `config --explain` runs (the explain output would print `docs.cli_command = ''` and would not print `docs.link_timeout_s`).
* If the section instead defines `link_timeout_s` in place of `cli_command`, commit 8209c908/09ebbddd was rewritten rather than copied as instructed, and B-docscheck-extractors' "`cli_command`" reader has no knob to read; the README claim of "228 knobs across 31 sections" (220 + the 8 enumerated knobs, `cli_command` included) is then wrong by one, since the docs section would contribute `link_timeout_s` as a ninth-or-substituted knob and the knob_added fragment set required by the release-manifest lint would not match the documented knobs.

Concretely, given a `Config` whose `docs` section is the one specified (`cli_command` present), line 1982ff of this snapshot produces a `docs` listing containing `docs.link_timeout_s = 10` and no `docs.cli_command`; snapshot comparison fails because the produced explain output differs in both directions (extra key, missing key). The change needs to show which of the two knob sets the code actually has, and make the golden, the README counts and the knob fragments ag

chunk_findings.detail: The new test configures `[docs] severity = "block"` together with a `lint_command` that cannot run (`"no-such-linter-xyz"`), then asserts both that the report is not clean / is blocking **and** that `out.exit == O.NOTHING` (the no-finding exit code, i.e. 0). That contradicts the exit contract this task is defined by: `Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 could not run (never 0) / 3 refused`. Here a configured check literally could not run and the report is explicitly not clean (`out.data["clean"] is False`) and blocking (`out.data["blocking"] is True`), so the run is exactly the "could not run"/refused case that must not be reported as 0; a CI job that inspects only the exit status of `ddflow docs check` would treat a blocking, could-not-run report as a pass. The test locks in that behaviour, so either the assertion should expect the non-zero outcome (2/3) or the implementation's exit mapping is wrong — the test as written enshrines exit 0 for the case the intent says must never be 0.

The new golden output for `["help"], 0` no longer just bumps the count (114 → 115) and appends `ddflow_docs` to a proper category. It appends a brand-new section whose header is the literal string `Unmapped — add a prefix to `_GROUPS``, with `ddflow_docs` nested underneath:

```

Unmapped — add a prefix to `_GROUPS`
